input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, licence, sell or use any product or service and to conduct business in any field or territory, and records that we have given no non-compete commitment. That satisfies the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is needed. No other clause imposes a competitive or field-of-use restraint on us: Section 2.1 confirms there is no purchase commitment, and the Section 13.4 use restrictions (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) are ordinary acceptable-use terms, expressly not limiting authorized testing or use of Customer Data and output. Section 2.2 (Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services) is a sourcing exclusivity commitment and belongs under the EXCLUSIVITY rule — it restricts who we buy from rather than what business we may operate or what we may build, so we do not double-flag it here; it should also be reconciled with the contrary acknowledgement in 12.3 when EXCLUSIVITY is addressed.
